column2: agreed merge:insertar, but "inserto" is also a real noun (an insert: film, advertising, mechanical); check how much of it is the noun
agreed merge:comisaría; comisar is a real verb (to confiscate) and comisaria/comisaría are two different words; check the merge target and whether a second word hides here
agreed merge:faja; fajar/fajarse is a real verb (to wrap; to fight, Latin America); check whether the verb is a real share
agreed merge:pie (misspelt pié/píe); piar is a real verb (to chirp); check whether any share is the verb
agreed merge:lustre; lustrar is a common real verb in Latin America (lustrar zapatos); check whether the verb is a real share
agreed merge:volver; "vuelto" is also a real noun (change, money: "el vuelto", Latin America); check whether the noun is a real share
agreed merge:amplio; the misaccented form may equally be amplía, from ampliar; check which word it is
agreed merge:alicate; alicatar is a real verb (to tile; alicatado); check whether the verb is a real share
agreed drop as English "more"; morar is a real Spanish verb (to dwell); check whether its real Spanish forms are enough to keep
agreed drop as a French loan; diaporama is in the academy's dictionary and used in Spain for a slide show
agreed drop as the place Pocitos; pocito is the ordinary diminutive of pozo, and a real common word stays even if many occurrences are a name
agreed drop as the society Mensa; mensa is a real colloquial word (feminine of menso, "silly", Mexico) and Latin "mensa" in liturgy
agreed drop as surname/place; vivar is a real common noun (warren, fish nursery) and a verb (to cheer, Latin America)
agreed drop as a hesitation sound; interjections that are their own lemma keep, and this may merge into a listed hmm or mmm
